stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and benefits from Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: TikTok employees said they knew about child safety issues, but execs failed to act
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: Internal TikTok employees reportedly warned leadership about significant child safety risks on the platform.
Concerns raised by staff included minors circumventing age restrictions and exposure to transactional sexual content.
The core issue highlighted is the alleged failure of TikTok executives to adequately address these internal safety warnings.

stories.title: Meta Muse exposes users' personal and business secrets when they share conversations
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Meta's Muse AI exhibits significant privacy vulnerabilities, allowing easy retrieval of user conversations.
A single query is sufficient to locate thousands of conversations based on their titles.
The story highlights critical security flaws in a major AI product, raising concerns about data exposure.

stories.title: OpenVLHarness: Real World Visual Agentic Tool-Use with Multimodal Memory
stories.author: Kai-Wei Chang
bullet_points: Introduces OpenVLHarness, a system designed for real-world visual agentic tool-use.
Addresses a key limitation of current Multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) where internal reasoning is insufficient for complex tasks.
Demonstrates that external tools, grounded perception, and interpretable outputs are necessary for significant performance gains on benchmarks.

stories.title: Text-to-Image Generative Modeling Without Language Pretraining
stories.author: Michael Poli
bullet_points: Introduces 'Halcyon,' a new family of multimodal autoregressive models designed for text-to-image generation without relying on large-scale language pretraining.
Halcyon achieves state-of-the-art performance (e.g., outperforming LlamaGen-XL/8) while requiring significantly less pretraining compute (18.2x less).
The model is trained entirely from scratch on GPIC, a dataset comprising 100M image-text pairs, challenging the necessity of massive language models in T2I.

stories.title: OpenVLHarness: Real World Visual Agentic Tool-Use with Multimodal Memory
stories.author: Kai-Wei Chang
bullet_points: Introduces OpenVLHarness, a system designed for real-world visual agentic tool-use.
Addresses the limitation of current Multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) where internal reasoning is insufficient for tasks requiring external evidence.
Demonstrates that simply increasing model inference budget provides only modest gains, necessitating grounded perception and tool integration.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1 model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation tasks, indicating its primary function as a large language model.
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors, suggesting modern implementation.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The model is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function.
The associated tags (transformers, llama, safetensors) confirm its relevance to the modern LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for running complex, multi-step tasks and tool-calling locally on user hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million in a new funding round.
Ollama currently serves a substantial developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance shows up to a 90% speed increase according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Spotify pulled 50 million AI slop and spam tracks from its recommendations
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Spotify has removed over 50 million AI-generated tracks deemed 'slop' or spam from its recommendations.
The platform is actively adjusting its recommendation algorithms to prioritize music created by human artists.
This move signals a growing industry effort to combat low-quality, mass-produced AI content in music streaming.

stories.title: Same Simulation, Different Evidence: Where Retrieved Tool Output Costs LLM Agents Accuracy
stories.author: Maziar Raissi
bullet_points: The study investigates how storing long tool outputs (e.g., from scientific simulators) outside the LLM context window affects agent accuracy.
Researchers used PHREEQC, a large-output geochemistry simulator, to test agents' performance on 158 verified questions.
The findings demonstrate that even when agents compute the correct answer, the method of handling large external tool outputs can introduce accuracy errors.

stories.title: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis
stories.author: Huaxiu Yao
bullet_points: Introduces WildAWM, a pipeline for synthesizing controllable environments for training computer-use agents (CUAs).
Addresses the challenge of scaling agent learning from simulation to real-world computer systems while mitigating security risks.
Marks a shift in agent learning from relying solely on human data toward interaction with complex, synthesized environments.

stories.title: MemT-1.0: Towards Memory-Native Evolution
stories.author: Feiyu Xiong
bullet_points: Introduces MemT-1.0, a new architecture for memory foundation models designed to internalize memory as a core computational capability.
The model utilizes Gated DeltaNet-2 with a stable token-level memory update mechanism for continuous information accumulation.
Scalability is addressed through the introduction of Mixture-of-Storage to enhance native memory capacity.

stories.title: OpenVLHarness: Real World Visual Agentic Tool-Use with Multimodal Memory
stories.author: Kai-Wei Chang
bullet_points: Introduces OpenVLHarness, a system designed for real-world visual agentic tool-use.
Addresses the limitation of current Multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) where internal reasoning is insufficient for complex tasks.
Demonstrates that external tools, grounded perception, and interpretable outputs are necessary for significant performance gains on benchmarks.

stories.title: Clef is available on Ollama's cloud
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Clef, a 27B multimodal decision model from Cloudflare, is now integrated with Ollama.
Users have the option to run the Clef model either locally or via Ollama's cloud service.
This integration expands the capabilities of Ollama by adding a powerful, large-scale multimodal model.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection's open-weight model, Beam, is now available on the Ollama platform.
Beam is specifically designed for complex tasks such as software engineering, reasoning, and agentic workflows.
The model is currently offered for free access through Ollama Cloud for a limited duration.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the deployment of AI agents using its cloud models.
The integration allows these agents to run securely within Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.
This combination addresses the need for safe and accessible deployment of AI agents.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama now integrates support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution of typed decisions.
Functionally, the models can answer yes/no questions, provide choices, and assign probabilities to options based on text input.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI services with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: The Gospel according to Peter (Thiel)
stories.author: David Gibson
bullet_points: Silicon Valley is experiencing a rise in apocalyptic worldviews regarding AI.
The current AI 'doom cycle' is being influenced by the philosophy of effective altruism (EA).
EA's influence is growing within the AI industry, impacting major players like Anthropic and safety watchdogs like METR.

stories.title: Adobe Lightroom mobile can now open closed eyes in photos with a simple tap
stories.author: Andrew Liszewski
bullet_points: Adobe Lightroom mobile now integrates generative AI to fix closed eyes in photos.
The feature is accessible via a single tap on iOS, iPadOS, and Android.
This represents a practical application of generative AI in consumer photo editing.

stories.title: Spotify’s new podcast memberships let you pay for extra perks
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: Spotify is rolling out a new 'Memberships' subscription feature for podcast creators.
This allows podcasters to monetize their content by offering fans exclusive perks.
Perks include bonus episodes, early access, and additional content, starting in 34 regions.

stories.title: Some Google Home Speakers caught downloading hundreds of gigs of data
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: A bug in some Google Home Speakers is causing continuous, large-scale data downloads (hundreds of GBs).
The issue was reported by users on platforms like Reddit and 9to5Google over the past week.
The suspected cause is a failure of the speakers to correctly download or install a firmware update.

stories.title: Japan launches mission to bring home a piece of the Martian moon Phobos
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: Japan is launching the MMX mission to retrieve a sample from Mars's moon, Phobos.
The mission's culmination is scheduled for 2029.
MMX is designed to attempt up to two landing operations on Phobos.

stories.title: Russian spacecraft maneuvers in "extreme proximity" to satellite used by Ukraine
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: A Russian spacecraft (Kosmos 2612) performed a maneuver near a satellite used by Ukraine (ICEYE-X36).
The maneuver involved closing to 'extreme proximity' between the two objects.
The event raises geopolitical and space security concerns regarding satellite proximity operations.

stories.title: Accused OpenAI spy had folder called “Saudi Gov Docs,” FBI says
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: FBI investigation reveals an ex-OpenAI engineer was accused of spying.
Evidence seized included a folder labeled "Saudi Gov Docs."
US authorities fear the Saudi government may assist the engineer in evading charges.

stories.title: Batteries help reduce emissions, but how do we reduce their emissions?
stories.author: Scott K. Johnson
bullet_points: The article addresses the environmental impact of batteries, despite their role in reducing emissions.
A key strategy discussed for reducing battery emissions is minimizing the overall number of batteries required.
This suggests a focus on efficiency and design optimization rather than solely on material sourcing.

stories.title: PSA: Patch your Plex media server before someone hacks it
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A researcher has identified a chain of four vulnerabilities affecting Plex media servers.
The news serves as a critical security advisory (PSA) urging users to patch their Plex installations immediately.
The vulnerability chain highlights the risk associated with running unpatched software in consumer-facing services.

stories.title: Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation
stories.author: Yujin Wang
bullet_points: The research addresses limitations in multimodal reinforcement learning (RLVR) by introducing On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD).
OPSD aims to provide dense, token-level error localization using a privileged teacher with an evidence-centered visual view.
A key challenge identified is the potential conflation of genuine visual evidence with artifacts from linguistic priors or response style.

stories.title: CoopUQ: Robust Multi-Robot Social Navigation via Uncertainty-Aware Cooperative Forecasting
stories.author: Jiachen Li
bullet_points: Introduces CoopUQ, a method for robust multi-robot social navigation.
Addresses limitations of single-robot RL in multi-robot settings, particularly concerning safety and efficiency.
Focuses on handling challenging real-world scenarios like occlusions and out-of-distribution (OOD) data through uncertainty-aware cooperative forecasting.

stories.title: Where is Physical RSI capability from? An Observational Scaling Law of LLM-as-policy
stories.author: Li Yi
bullet_points: The paper investigates the mechanisms and scaling behavior of physical Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) in Large Language Models (LLMs).
A new evaluation framework, PhysRSI-eval, is introduced to quantify physical RSI using a five-axis metric (e.g., First-Attempt Performance, Efficiency).
The research presents the 'Physical Barrel Hypothesis,' suggesting different capabilities might be constrained by specific factors during physical interaction tasks.

stories.title: WeAct: Dynamic Weight Switching as Agent Actions
stories.author: Shuyan Zhou
bullet_points: Addresses catastrophic forgetting in long-horizon AI agents when learning heterogeneous capabilities.
Introduces WeAct (Weight-level Internal Actions) to dynamically switch between independent capabilities during execution.
Overcomes limitations of conventional joint training and static adapter merging by allowing parameter configuration changes mid-trajectory.

stories.title: Train An Imaginative Agent
stories.author: Haiwen Feng
bullet_points: Introduces 'Agentic Imagination' (Agima), a new training framework for AI agents.
Agima enables agents to 'imagine' the consequences of their actions before execution, addressing issues like irreversible actions.
The framework trains a single omni-model to propose actions, generate outcome images, and reason about them.

stories.title: AnyGoal: On World Model Generalization Beyond Expert Rollouts
stories.author: David Klindt
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical challenge of world model generalization beyond the specific data seen during expert training.
World models are important for enabling agents to plan and simulate actions within an environment.
The study investigates the under-explored relationship between data coverage, dynamics generalization, and planning performance.

stories.title: LatComm: Reusable Context Compression for Latent Communication between Large Language Models
stories.author: Weijie Zhao
bullet_points: LatComm addresses the inefficiency of repeatedly processing large, shared contexts when chaining multiple LLMs.
The method aims to create a compact, reusable context representation that is understandable across different LLMs.
It improves upon existing compression and latent communication techniques by satisfying multiple required properties simultaneously.

stories.title: Kronecker Delta Rule for Long Context Linear Attention
stories.author: Sepp Hochreiter
bullet_points: Introduces KronLSTM, a new linear attention architecture leveraging the Kronecker Delta Rule.
KronLSTM features a memory-revision mechanism that corrects associations with minimal interference to stored data.
The architecture is specifically designed to improve performance in long-context sequence modeling tasks.

stories.title: CoopUQ: Robust Multi-Robot Social Navigation via Uncertainty-Aware Cooperative Forecasting
stories.author: Jiachen Li
bullet_points: Introduces CoopUQ, a method for robust multi-robot social navigation using reinforcement learning.
Addresses key challenges in multi-robot systems, specifically safety and efficiency in human-shared environments.
Focuses on handling uncertainty, occlusions, and out-of-distribution (OOD) scenarios through cooperative forecasting.

stories.title: WeAct: Dynamic Weight Switching as Agent Actions
stories.author: Shuyan Zhou
bullet_points: Addresses catastrophic forgetting in long-horizon AI agents that need diverse capabilities.
Introduces WeAct (Weight-level Internal Actions) to dynamically switch between specialized model weights during execution.
Overcomes limitations of static parameter configurations used in conventional joint training and adapter merging.

stories.title: Supervised Learning with Quantum Hamiltonian Embeddings
stories.author: Kunal Sharma
bullet_points: Introduces 'quantum Hamiltonian embeddings' as a new supervised learning framework.
Aims to bridge the gap between classical training data and quantum computing models.
Addresses the current limitation of lacking provable performance guarantees in general quantum ML.

stories.title: ProteinGeoBench: Frontier Structural-Biology Agents Are Fluent at Lookup but Lost in Geometry
stories.author: James B. Golden
bullet_points: ProteinGeoBench is a new benchmark suite (131 tasks) designed to test frontier AI agents on protein structure tasks.
The study reveals a performance gap: models excel at retrieving structural metadata but struggle with accurate geometric computation from coordinates.
The research investigates whether this performance gap is inherent to the models or due to the evaluation setup.

stories.title: Can It Actually Work? Synthesizing Functional CAD Mechanisms
stories.author: Zhen Liu
bullet_points: LLM agents can generate visually plausible CAD designs, but these often lack functional correctness.
The research focuses on 'functional CAD design,' where agents must satisfy specific physical requirements through iterative simulation.
Verifying functional requirements is complex because multiple distinct mechanisms can achieve the same intended function.

stories.title: WeAct: Dynamic Weight Switching as Agent Actions
stories.author: Shuyan Zhou
bullet_points: Addresses catastrophic forgetting in long-horizon AI agents that need diverse capabilities.
Introduces WeAct (Weight-level Internal Actions) to dynamically switch between independent capabilities during execution.
Overcomes limitations of static parameter configurations used in conventional joint training and adapter merging.

stories.title: LatComm: Reusable Context Compression for Latent Communication between Large Language Models
stories.author: Weijie Zhao
bullet_points: LatComm addresses the inefficiency of passing large, redundant contexts between multiple Large Language Models (LLMs).
It introduces a novel context representation designed to be compact, reusable across different queries, and understandable by various LLMs.
The method aims to reduce computational overhead by avoiding the need for receiving models to re-process the entire context for every new question.

stories.title: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis
stories.author: Huaxiu Yao
bullet_points: Introduces WildAWM, a pipeline designed to synthesize controllable environments for training computer-use agents (CUAs).
Addresses the challenge of scaling agent learning from human data to real-world interaction while mitigating security risks.
Represents a shift in AI research towards agents learning through direct interaction with complex, simulated environments.

stories.title: KEEP-Bench: Evaluating Evidence Preservation in Context Compression
stories.author: Nanyun Peng
bullet_points: Introduces KEEP-Bench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate 'faithfulness' in context compression techniques.
Addresses a critical limitation in current evaluations where standard QA metrics fail to detect information loss during compression.
Focuses on the problem of information bottlenecks in long-context efficiency, particularly concerning evidence preservation.

stories.title: RefCraft: Benchmarking Visual-Reference-Conditioned Agentic Generation through Web Development
stories.author: Shuai Bai
bullet_points: The paper introduces RefCraft, a new benchmark for evaluating AI agents that incorporate visual references during generation.
It addresses a gap in current benchmarks, which often focus only on text-to-webpage generation or visual reconstruction, ignoring real-world workflows.
The study uses webpage development as a practical, evaluable setting to test the crucial capability of visual-reference-conditioned agentic generation.

stories.title: MemT-1.0: Towards Memory-Native Evolution
stories.author: Feiyu Xiong
bullet_points: Introduces MemT-1.0, a new architecture for memory foundation models designed to internalize memory as a core computational capability.
Utilizes Gated DeltaNet-2 and a stable token-level memory update mechanism for continuous information accumulation.
Scales native memory capacity through the introduction of a Mixture-of-Storage component.

stories.title: DeepSeek just open-sourced its inference engine
stories.author: ggcr
bullet_points: DeepSeek has made its inference engine publicly available (open-sourced).
This release contributes to the growing trend of open-sourcing foundational AI components.
The availability of the engine allows researchers and developers to inspect and build upon the core inference mechanism.

stories.title: Publish fake stats, get cited in LLMs
stories.author: robtherobber
bullet_points: The article discusses the vulnerability of Large Language Models (LLMs) to misinformation.
It highlights that LLMs can be manipulated into citing fabricated statistics.
This points to a significant issue regarding the reliability and trustworthiness of AI-generated information.

stories.title: Your agent's retry bug isn't an AI problem. It's a distributed-systems problem with an LLM on top.
stories.author: cyclopt_dimitrisk
bullet_points: The article argues that common agent failures (like retry bugs) are rooted in distributed systems, not the LLM itself.
It critiques the oversimplification of agent demos, which often only showcase the 'happy path' (successful tool execution).
This highlights a critical engineering challenge: building robust AI agents requires solving complex distributed systems problems.

stories.title: Stress-Testing Gemini 4 Argon: Building a 3D Flutter Kart Game in 15 Prompts with Zero Assets
stories.author: leehack
bullet_points: The article explores using frontier AI models (specifically Gemini 4 Argon) for complex, non-standard coding tasks.
It demonstrates building a 3D Flutter game using only 15 prompts and zero pre-existing assets.
The piece highlights a limitation in current AI coding benchmarks, which often focus only on standard web applications or CRUD interfaces.
